newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa processors running down cover.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa processors running down cover.

text.p: German cocoa consumers made only small outright purchases because futures were falling and the pound was too strong against the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
"It's not a winning combination from the trader's point of view," one said.
"The industry is running down its stocks but obviously can afford to do so, trade has been routine for at least a week and a half."
Only some cocoa butter and mass were sold for Nov/Dec.
London March cocoa was at 938 stg, up five, at 1620 GMT as the market rebounded from lows set earlier this week.
Traders said arrivals data in West African ports were being closely monitoried but it would take another four weeks before a clearer picture would emerge.
Ghana purchases of 32,130 tonnes, up in the first week of the marketing season from 22,834 tonnes last year, were no indicator of higher supplies.
"The figure looks higher but shipments started later this year," one trader said.
Local bean prices were 0.03 marks/kg down on the week at 2.20 for Nov/Dec and at 2.26 marks for first quarter, down 0.01.
The cocoa butter ratio eased by one point to 2.78-2.80 for 1996 dates. Implied butter prices liquid ex-works were at 6.27-6.28 marks, down 0.09-0.10 on the week.
The first quarter ratio was at 2.70-2.72, with mark prices at 6.27-6.28.
Sterling was fixed in Frankfurt on Wednesday at 2.4903 marks. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
